analysis:
Examined scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py head lines 469-994. This is an offline unit test for the CI workflow, not provider runtime code. It does not touch the provider/coordinator WebSocket, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, the prefix cache storage (T-041), or the add-on hold socket. No threat-model asset or trust boundary changes.

The security-relevant intent is CI supply-chain hygiene, and the added tests strengthen it:
- Actions are pinned by SHA (CHECKOUT, CACHE_RESTORE, CACHE_SAVE).
- Caches are saved only on push to master or dev, never from PRs (test_only_pushes_to_master_and_dev_save_caches, lines 788-813). This limits PR cache poisoning.
- Checkouts use persist-credentials: false, so tokens are not saved into the cached .git (lines 844-850).
- A damaged restored .git is discarded (VALIDATE_GIT, tested at 856-887).
- The parity lane and cluster-metadata job are asserted to carry no secrets, no continue-on-error and no backend credentials (lines 699-700, 765-774).
- Sparse checkout skips only .gz evidence archives and landing mp4 files (lines 889-916). The test confirms that the report a provider test hashes and the Swift test fixtures are kept.

The subprocess calls use fixed argv lists, temp dirs and no shell interpolation of untrusted input. The one bash -c call runs a command read from the repo's own workflow. That is acceptable in a test harness.

Remaining limits: I did not see the workflow YAML, the composite action, or the first part of the file. The tests' assertions are only as good as the actual workflow they check. The patch excerpt was truncated. No regression is identified in the supplied units.
